pl-l4d7c5-d1e115.summary: Holds that confirmation must not be repeated, like baptism and orders, since no sacrament must be wronged, which is thought to happen when what must not be repeated is repeated.
claims: Repeating an unrepeatable sacrament wrongs it.

pl-l4d7c5-d1e118.summary: Notes that whether some or none can be repeated is a question.

pl-l4d7c5-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine on baptism and orders: both are sacraments and given by a certain consecration, at baptism and at ordination, so neither may be repeated in the Catholic Church, since neither must be wronged. The same must be held without doubt of confirmation; whether others can or should be repeated will be discussed later.
claims: Baptism and orders are given by consecration and not repeated.

pl-l4d7c5.summary: Holds that confirmation, like baptism and orders, must not be repeated, since repeating what must not be repeated wrongs the sacrament. Whether other sacraments can be repeated is a question for later; Augustine says baptism and orders, given by a consecration, may not be repeated in the Catholic Church, and the same must be held of confirmation.
claims: Confirmation, baptism, and orders are not repeated.
Repeating an unrepeatable sacrament wrongs it.
Whether other sacraments can be repeated is treated later.
